amundsen-gjoa-005.description: A hand-coloured lantern slide of Roald Amundsen aboard the Gjoa, inscribed within the image 'Roald Amundsen ombord Gjoa. April 1903' - taken at Christiania two months before the ship sailed for the Northwest Passage.

amundsen-gjoa-007.description: Greenlandic Inuit aboard the Gjoa during her call at Godhavn (Qeqertarsuaq) on Disko in late July 1903, where the expedition took on dogs, sledges and sealskin clothing before crossing Melville Bay.

amundsen-gjoa-008.description: Drift ice photographed from the deck of the Gjoa. The photograph carries no date; the crossing of Melville Bay in the first half of August 1903, which Roald Amundsen called the most difficult stretch of the whole passage for a ship as small as his, is the likeliest occasion, and the position given here is that crossing.

amundsen-gjoa-010.description: Christmas aboard the Gjoa in her first winter at Gjoahavn (Uqsuqtuuq), 24 December 1903. The expedition's own plate of the same evening is amundsen-gjoa-048.

amundsen-gjoa-021.description: The Gjoa's crew on board at Nome, photographed by Frank H. Nowell, the photographer of the Nome gold rush. His caption on the image reads: 'Capt. Amundsen and his crew on board the GJOA, Nome, Sep 1st, 1906. Photo by F.H. Nowell, Nome, Alaska, Copyright 1906.' It is NOWELL 252 in the University of Washington's Nowell collection.

amundsen-gjoa-037.description: The scanned page images of volume II of Roald Amundsen's The North West Passage, 27.8 MB, as printed by Archibald Constable in 1908: the Netsilik chapters of Part II with their photographic plates and the portraits of named individuals, the passage west, King Point, the journey to Eagle, Nome, and Godfred Hansen's supplement on the Victoria Island survey. The plates carry Amundsen's own printed captions, and the printed page is the authority for any quotation or name from this volume.

amundsen-gjoa-038.description: A replica of the ship's bell recovered from HMS Erebus, on display in the Nattilik Heritage Centre at Uqsuqtuuq (Gjoa Haven); the year 1845 is visible near the top, and the photographer's own caption calls it a replica. The wreck was found in 2014 in Wilmot and Crampton Bay after Inuit oral testimony - gathered over a lifetime by Louie Kamookak of this hamlet and, before him, by Rae, Hall, Schwatka and Roald Amundsen - put the searchers in the right water. The object stands in the hamlet named for Amundsen's ship.
